In dockerized_labs/sensitive_data_exposure/dataexposure/views.py, `login_required` is applied to EXACTLY TWO views — `profile_view` (line 68) and `api_data_view` (line 86). `all_users_data_view` (def at line 112) has NO decorator applied and NO in-body `request.user.is_authenticated` check anywhere in its body (lines 112-132 contain only a list literal, the ORM call, the dict build and the JsonResponse). It calls `UserData.objects.all()` (line 120) and returns `JsonResponse({'users': all_users_data})` (line 132) where each record is `{'username', 'credit_card', 'ssn', 'api_key'}` (line 121). The route is registered unauthenticated in dataexposure/urls.py line 4 as `path('api/all-users/', views.all_users_data_view, name='all_users_data')`. Any unauthenticated remote attacker GETs /api/all-users/ and receives every user's credit card number, SSN and API key.

MISSING ENCRYPTION-AT-REST for sensitive fields. The `UserData` model stores payment and government-identity data in plaintext `CharField` columns with no encryption, hashing, tokenization or masking: `credit_card = models.CharField(max_length=16)` (models.py line 6), `ssn = models.CharField(max_length=9)` (line 7), `api_key = models.CharField(max_length=32)` (line 8). The confirming migration 0001_initial.py lines 21-23 creates them as bare `models.CharField(max_length=16/9/32)`. No EncryptedCharField, Fernet, cryptography, or django-fields encryption wrapper appears anywhere in the scan. Combined with lead #1 (unauthenticated `api/all-users/`) and DB compromise, this exposes raw PANs and SSNs.

MISSING SESSION-TOKEN INTEGRITY (no signature/MAC) plus DEBUG-MODE RCE in the Flask broken-auth lab. dockerized_labs/broken_auth_lab/app.py builds its session cookie as pure reversible encoding with NO HMAC/signature: `session_token = base64.b64encode(f"{username}:{datetime.now()}".encode()).decode()` (line 45), then sets it with no flags at line 49 `response.set_cookie('session', session_token, max_age = 30*24*60*60)` and line 51. On the read side it simply trusts it: `username = base64.b64decode(session_token).decode().split(':')[0]` (line 111) with only a `not session_token` emptiness check at line 106 — no signature verification step exists. An attacker base64-encodes `admin:<any date>` and becomes admin. Compounding: `app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=5000, debug=True)` (line 123) exposes the Werkzeug interactive debugger console on all interfaces → unauthenticated RCE; and the password-reset token uses MD5 of guessable material `hashlib.md5(f"{email}:{datetime.now()}".encode()).hexdigest()` (line 86).

MISSING CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY-SECURE RANDOMNESS for secret material — the non-CSPRNG `random` module (Mersenne Twister, fully reconstructable from observed output) is used instead of `secrets`/`os.urandom`. `generate_api_key` builds the stored API key with `''.join(random.choices(chars, k=16))` at dockerized_labs/sensitive_data_exposure/dataexposure/views.py line 42 (module imported as plain `import random`, line 9); this method is reachable_from_entry=true at hop_distance=2 and is the 3rd-highest-centrality first-party method in the whole reachable call graph (centrality 2.219e-5), i.e. a chokepoint whose weakness propagates to every issued key. Likewise `''.join(random.choices(string.ascii_uppercase + string.ascii_lowercase, k=10))` at introduction/views.py line 680 in `gentckt` (reachable, hop 2, centrality 9.76e-6) generates ticket identifiers. No `secrets.token_hex`, `secrets.token_urlsafe`, or `os.urandom` call exists anywhere in the scan. An attacker who collects a few outputs predicts subsequent API keys / ticket IDs.

The project's standard authentication protection is commented out on a live, URL-routed API endpoint. introduction/apis.py:60-61 reads `@csrf_exempt` / `# @authentication_decorator` / `def log_function_checker(request):` — the auth decorator is present but DISABLED by a comment, while the CSRF exemption is kept active. This is a reverted protection: `authentication_decorator` (defined introduction/views.py:76) is the established project-wide guard with 40 resolved call sites across views.py and mitre.py, so this endpoint is a deliberate opt-out. The endpoint is routed at introduction/urls.py:83 (`path("2021/discussion/A9/api", apis.log_function_checker, ...)`) and is marked reachable_from_entry=true.

An authorization check is explicitly acknowledged as missing by an in-code comment on a live route serving a secret. `a1_broken_access_lab3_secret` (introduction/views.py:837) contains the comment `# no checking applied here` exactly where the privilege check belongs, then unconditionally returns `render(request, 'Lab_2021/A1_BrokenAccessControl/secret.html')`. It only verifies `request.user.is_authenticated` — any logged-in user, not just the admin. The sibling view `a1_broken_access_lab_3` (views.py:822) does compute an admin role (`elif username == 'admin' and password == 'admin_pass': ... 'admin': True`), proving an admin/non-admin distinction exists that this endpoint declines to enforce. The hedge comment is direct evidence the author knew the protection was absent. Routed at introduction/urls.py:60 as `broken_access_control/secret`, reachable_from_entry=true.

Password hashing is replaced by a home-rolled weakening of SHA-256 instead of a password KDF. introduction/utility.py:58 defines `def customHash(password): return hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest()[::-1]` — a single unsalted, uniterated SHA-256 whose hex digest is merely string-reversed (`[::-1]`). The reversal is pure obfuscation that adds no cryptographic strength (it is trivially undone), while the real protections — a per-user salt and an adaptive KDF such as PBKDF2/bcrypt/argon2, which Django provides out of the box — are absent. A function deliberately named `customHash` that substitutes a reversible transform for a KDF is a protection replaced by a decorative stand-in. The function has 1 resolved caller in the graph.

Known-vulnerable component whose exploit precondition is present in-graph: Dependency node `Werkzeug ==2.1.2` is declared, and the Flask lab `dockerized_labs/broken_auth_lab/app.py:123` starts the server with the literal `debug = True` -> `app.run(host = '0.0.0.0', port = 5000, debug = True)`. Werkzeug < 3.0.3 is affected by CVE-2024-34069: the interactive debugger can be driven to remote code execution by an attacker who can get a victim to issue requests, and the debugger is only mounted when debug=True. The bind to 0.0.0.0 exposes it beyond localhost. Werkzeug 2.1.2 is additionally behind CVE-2023-25577 (multipart form-data resource-exhaustion DoS, fixed 2.2.3), CVE-2023-23934 (cookie-parsing confusion) and CVE-2024-49767 (multipart resource exhaustion). VERIFIER NOTE: version pin and the debug=True / 0.0.0.0 literals are graph-grounded; CVE mapping is from my knowledge.

Pattern-in-data crash: in `mitre_lab_17_api` (introduction/mitre.py) the literal `pattern = "STATE SERVICE.*\\n\\n"` (line 245) is matched against attacker-influenced subprocess output and the match list is indexed unconditionally at [0]: line 246 `re.findall(pattern, res, re.DOTALL)[0][14:-2].split('\n')`, reachable_from_entry=true. `res` is the stdout of `subprocess.Popen("nmap " + request.POST.get('ip'), shell=True)` (lines 240-242, 233). An attacker supplying any `ip` for which nmap emits no "STATE SERVICE" table (unroutable host, blank value, a flag, or a shell-metacharacter payload that changes the command) makes `re.findall` return an empty list, so `[0]` raises IndexError in a view with no try/except — an unhandled 500 / availability defect driven purely by the literal failing to match. (The `.*` under re.DOTALL has no nested quantifier and a literal prefix, so this is NOT catastrophic backtracking.) Note the same lines carry a separate, more severe shell command-injection issue that is outside Shape D.

(2) zipp CVE-2024-5569 requires parsing a crafted zip archive; there is no zipfile or zipp usage anywhere in app code (zipp is a transitive importlib-metadata dep doing internal zip-path resolution, never fed attacker-controlled archives).
